intro.text: The council of guilds that rules Lossand. Its eight members, each called a Taisha, speak for the nation's eight Professions.

description.text: Most Profession guilds take in many smaller trades: the Draft of Artisans, for example, covers painters but also carpenters, cobblers and doctors.
Each Taisha is styled Lord or Lady, and whoever leads the council also takes the title High. At present that is the High Judge.

The council sits in a triangular chamber in the Hall of Judgement. The Taishin occupy a raised dais along the back wall, with seats for Kelzin and others along the other two sides and the entrance at the point facing them. A steward records each party and announces speakers, and no new party is called until the floor has been yielded.
Nilto, called the Lord Beggar, holds no seat or vote, yet he carries as much weight as any Taisha thanks to his work for the poor and those without a Profession.

items.text: After the Diem's massacre in the Kerla, the council met to disband the Sand Masters' Profession, many members having their own reasons. Every Taisha but Lord Admiral Delius voted to do so.

Acting Lord Mastrell Kenton argued that two laws of the council's charter made the vote void. High Judge Heelis agreed the laws said so but treated the vote as preliminary; since it stood six to one, and an acting Lord Mastrell cannot vote, only a unanimous vote could reverse it.
Once the duel at the Diem was over, Kenton called for the deciding vote, and the council chose unanimously to keep the Profession of Sand Masters.
When there is no Lord Mastrell, the seat seems to pass to the Diem's most senior mastrell.
For about a century the Lords Mastrell held a huge, unpayable debt over the Lords Merchant and used it to make them do as they were told.
The Lord Mastrell runs the Diem and must approve every promotion beyond acolent. Kenton now holds the seat.
Drile, a demoted mastrell far stronger than Kenton, challenged him for it, and the two fought a duel before the vote. Afterwards Heelis confirmed Kenton as Lord Mastrell.
With Drile beside him, Kenton set the Diem on a different course from its past.
The Lady Judge, currently Heelis, heads the Hall of Judgement, leads Lossand's trackts and judges, and has the last word on the law.
As the council's present leader she presides over its meetings with the title High Judge.

For the final vote Heelis, admitting she favoured the Diem and wanting an impartial vote, handed her vote to Ais as someone set against it. Moved by what Kenton had done for her family, Ais put aside her Kerztian dislike of sand mastery and voted for the Diem.

Lord General Raagent had fallen under the crime lord Sharezan's control and reached out to Senior Trackt Ais for help breaking free. The meeting was found out and became a trap; both escaped, but Raagent was then found dead in the Tower's wine cellar, killed through his fear of the dark.
The Lord General leads Lossand's soldiers from the Tower Garrison. The seat seems to be inherited, and Aarik now holds it.
Kenton asked Aarik to take his father's place and back the Diem; Aarik agreed reluctantly and voted for it.

Lord Admiral Delius voted to keep the Diem only because Lord Merchant Vey voted against it. He promised Kenton his support, since he always votes against Vey, who as a Kerztian will never back the Diem.

Delius threw a party for the new Lord Mastrell, partly to meet Duchess Khrissalla but mainly to provoke the Kelzin shipowners, who hoped the Diem's end would win favour with the A'kar and ease the embargoes on the Helm's trade.

The seat heads the Helm in name only. The Shipowners' Circle holds the real power, and a new Lord Admiral loses all property, receiving just a ship when needed, a house and food and drink. The Circle uses the post to rein in anyone too successful or disobedient.

When the Circle removed Delius for backing the Diem, he signed papers taking its fleet as his own and threatened to block Kezare's port for a month. He promised to lift the threat if they made Lokkall Lord Admiral, then kept Lokkall's forfeited property, to be returned once Lokkall voted for the Diem.
Prompted by Delius, Lord Admiral Lokkall voted to keep the Diem without reservation.
The Lord Merchant heads the Guild, Lossand's banking Profession, from the Golden Market. Vey holds the seat.
The seat goes to the Guild's richest member, who takes on all of the last holder's wealth and debts.

About a century before Vey, Lord Merchant Hennin lost the money in a Lord Mastrell's private account through bad investments. The Diem's tributes kept going into the account and its interest grew until the debt could never be repaid.
Instead of calling in the debt, Kenton forgave it, earning Vey's respect and his vote.
The Lord Farmer, currently Gennel, heads the Field from the Farmers Congress, leading Lossand's farming, its Kelzin landholders and its quotas.
Gennel voted against the Diem at first. Like Vey he is Kerztian, and he generally appears to take his cue from Vey.
In the final vote he backed the Diem without saying why, apparently once more following Vey.
The Lord Artisan voted to disband the Diem in the first vote.
Rite, the Lord Artisan, is elected by his Professions' members and leads Lossand's makers from the Artisan Central Studio, overseeing the Draft.

Rite resented the law letting mastrells take goods and services unpaid. Once Kenton, advised by Khrissalla, promised sand masters' services to the Draft and to settle the 1,500,000 lak the Diem owed, Rite agreed to back it.
Saying his terms had been met and the debt paid, Rite voted to keep the Diem.
The Lady Mason voted to disband the Diem in the first vote.
She heads the Company, Lossand's builders, from the Mason Headquarters; her name is not given.
She voted for the Diem in the end, saying it had shown it could be useful and adaptable, chiefly because Kenton's sand saved several workers when a building collapsed.
